summary: Timebound GCP->AWS federated broker role for MLOps notebook cluster access
description:
Issue summary:
The MLOps team needs temporary access for a set of GCP-hosted notebook sessions to an AWS analytics account (read-only S3 + limited EMR query access) to debug a data skew that only reproduces in the analytics cluster.

Impact:
- Blocking interactive debugging of live dataflows that are currently failing post-deployment.
- Delays in triage for an internal investigation; affects two engineers for up to 48 hours.

Request:
Provision a timebound federated role/broker in the AWS analytics account that can be assumed via our GCP Workload Identity Pool (or equivalent OIDC path). Bindings should grant a least-privilege policy targeted to: s3:GetObject (specific prefixes), athena:StartQueryExecution (read-only query), and CloudWatch Logs Read (query only). Role must have an automatic expiration (7 days) and an explicit revocation method in the runbook.

Background and constraints:
- Originating identity: GCP service account: mlops-notebooks@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com (not user creds).
- Preferred mechanism: Workload Identity Federation -> sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity OR AWS STS AssumeRole via OIDC if required by security.
- Must follow existing org guardrails: MFA not required for service accounts, but Security wants audit events and tagged role session names including job/notebook id.
- No permanent cross-account keys allowed.

Desired expiration: 2026-03-17 (7 days from start).

Approval path: Request approved by MLOps lead (Riley Chen) and InfoSec reviewer (Asha Mehta) before prod rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Engineers can assume the role from the specified GCP service account and successfully run example athena query and S3 GET to the specific test prefix.
- Role session audit logs (CloudTrail) show federated principal and session name.
- Expiration policy verified and documented in internal runbook.
steps_to_reproduce: From staging notebook, run aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity using current OIDC token -> receive AccessDeniedException: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity denied
Attempt to access s3://analytics-prod/redwood/events/2026/03/01 -> 403 Forbidden in notebook kernel
CLI test from GCP shell using gcloud auth print-identity-token and curl to AWS STS endpoint shows 401/403 error with 'Invalid identity token' occasionally.
logs: 2026-03-09T16:02:14Z - sts.amazonaws.com - AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity - AccessDenied - User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/SomeRole/SomeSession - Message: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
2026-03-09T16:04:03Z - notebook-kernel - S3 GET - 403 Forbidden - Key: analytics/events/2026/03/01/eventlog.json
2026-03-09T16:05:10Z - gcloud - identity token payload - aud mismatch: expected arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-gcp-broker
investigation_notes: 03/10 - Initial triage: Request received from MLOps. Confirmed failing auth path and reproduced 403 from notebook using service account token.

03/11 - SRE checked AWS role trust policy; found trust currently configured for an internal CI OIDC provider only, not the staging workload-identity pool. Candidate fix: add staging pool provider ARN to trust with exact condition on token.sub and token.aud.

03/11 - Security flagged requirement for session naming convention: session must include 'notebook:<notebook-id>' and request explicit CloudTrail tags. Will require role policy tag/session tags in AssumeRole call from GCP side.

03/12 - Created draft IAM policy for least privilege (s3 get to prefix, athena StartQueryExecution read-only, logs:FilterLogEvents). Draft stored at: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/MLOPS-Access-Patterns#draft-policy
comments: Diego Ramos (03/10): Opening request — MLOps needs short-term access to debug analytics. Attached logs and target prefixes. Marking as timebound.

Priya Nandakumar (03/11): I looked at the AWS trust policy. Staging workload identity pool not whitelisted. I can add a staging principal but want Security confirmation on session naming and tags before prod change.
Asha Mehta (InfoSec) (03/11): Security OK with WIF for staging if role session naming and CloudTrail tagging enforced. Approve staging role for 7 days. Prod requires additional review.
Riley Chen (MLOps lead) (03/12): Approved for staging 7-day window. Please include notebook id in session name. Will coordinate to run tests after role is available.
resolution: Staging federated role created in aws-analytics account named 'redwood-gcp-notebook-broker-staging' with trust relationship to staging workload identity pool and condition on token.aud. Role has inline least-privilege policy and session tagging enforced. Expiration window set to 7 days (automated tag + scheduled alert to revoke). Pending: Security to approve prod path and CloudOps to add runbook steps for manual revocation. Testing checklist passed for staging on 2026-03-12.
next_steps: Expire and audit role on 2026-03-17; confirm no lingering sessions.
Create follow-up ticket for prod trust onboarding and formal security sign-off (owner: Priya).
Add automation to rotate policy and notify MLOps when role is provisioned (owner: CloudOps).
